title: The Garden of Junebug Creek Anew
premise: Wendell Zhou, a widowed single father running Junebug Creek's only bookshop, agrees to a fake date with returning hometown lawyer Marisol Vega to survive his mother's reunion weekend. What begins as theater deepens into real feeling, until Marisol's investigation into the hit-and-run that killed Wendell's wife threatens to expose a truth the town's most beloved family buried—and Wendell must choose between loyalty to the people who sheltered him and justice for the woman he lost. When the evidence finally surfaces, Wendell forgives himself for the guilt he carried, Marisol brings the case before an unconventional town tribunal when the statute of limitations looms, and the two choose each other openly at the rebuilt garden behind the bookshop.
about_author: F. M. Amberdale is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who spent a decade recommending love stories by day and drafting one by lamplight after closing. They write romances about people who mistake timing for fate.

chapters.title: The Reunion Letter
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A cream envelope announces the Zhou family reunion—first since his wife Lian's death—and his mother's note assumes he'll bring 'someone.' Wendell, raising eight-year-old Junie alone above the bookshop, drafts three refusals and burns none of them. Emotional beat: quiet dread dressed as routine, the ache of being seen as incomplete.

chapters.title: Marisol Comes Home
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. After eleven years away, attorney Marisol Vega returns to Junebug Creek to settle her grandmother's estate and reopen an old case file she stole from a courthouse box. She wanders into the bookshop for a map of the town she no longer recognizes. Emotional beat: homecoming as estrangement; two guarded strangers circling the same grief from opposite sides.

chapters.title: A Proposal Over Paperbacks
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marisol mentions, half-joking, that she needs a plus-one for her own family dinner; Wendell blurts that he needs one worse. They negotiate terms on a napkin: no feelings, no questions about the past. Emotional beat: comic relief with an undertow—both are lying, mostly to themselves.

chapters.title: The Zhou Table
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The reunion luncheon: Aunties interrogating, Junie charming everyone, Marisol improvising a courtship history so specific it startles Wendell himself. His mother watches too closely. Emotional beat: performance becoming intimacy; Wendell realizes he hasn't laughed like this since Lian died.

chapters.title: Dessert and Complications
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. By dessert the fake date feels dangerously real, and Marisol's aunt lets slip that the Vega family knew the driver in Lian's accident. Marisol leaves early, shaken—her stolen case file has a name on it she grew up loving. Emotional beat: the fake-date pact cracks under the weight of what she's hiding.

chapters.title: Junie's Question
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Junie asks why Mommy's garden died and whether new people are allowed to grow there. Wendell deflects with a bedtime story but lies awake confronting his guilt: he was driving the other car that night, unhurt, and never stopped blaming himself. Emotional beat: grief reframed as self-punishment.

chapters.title: The Second Date Nobody Planned
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Rain traps them in the shop after closing; inventory becomes conversation becomes almost-kiss, interrupted by Junie's nightlight emergency. They agree, stiffly, to keep things 'as contracted.' Emotional beat: longing denied aloud, confirmed in every gesture.

chapters.title: What the File Says
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Alone with the stolen file, Marisol confirms the driver was Caleb Ashford, son of the family whose charity saved Junebug Creek—and that her own grandfather helped bury it. Her motive sharpens: justice outside the law, because the law already failed once. Emotional beat: loyalty to blood versus loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: The Ashford Gala
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The Ashfords host their annual benefactor gala; Wendell caters the used-book donation table and watches Caleb charm the room. Caleb is kind to Junie, generous to the shop—the man who killed Lian is the town's saint. Emotional beat: nausea of proximity; Wendell nearly tells Marisol everything and can't.

chapters.title: Terms Renegotiated
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marisol, needing access to Ashford records, asks Wendell to extend the fake relationship into Ashford circles. He agrees, hating the transactional taste of it, while privately the contract has already expired in his heart. Emotional beat: complicity deepening; both now using each other for secrets neither will name.

chapters.title: Garden Restoration
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Junie and Marisol begin rebuilding Lian's ruined garden behind the shop without asking permission. Wendell's fury at the trespass reveals itself as terror—of memory being tended by someone new. Emotional beat: the midpoint rupture; he orders Marisol out, then stands alone among the turned soil.

chapters.title: The Mirror Chapter
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, intimate and interior. A sleepless night becomes a reckoning: Wendell confronts the person in the mirror, admitting he chose silence about that night not to protect Junie but to protect himself from blame. He writes Lian a letter he can't send. Emotional beat: the forgiveness arc turns inward first.

chapters.title: Marisol's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol comes to apologize and finds Wendell's unsent letter open on the counter—she learns he witnessed the accident. She flees before confessing her own secret, now certain the truth will destroy him twice. Emotional beat: dramatic irony tightening; love and deception fully entangled.

chapters.title: The Witness Nobody Called
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell tracks down the retired deputy who worked the accident, learning the case was closed in a single afternoon and that Marisol has been asking the same questions. Betrayal and hope arrive together: someone else believes it wasn't his fault. Emotional beat: anger as the doorway to relief.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Creek
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wendell demands the truth; Marisol gives it whole—the Ashford name, her grandfather's cover-up, the statute of limitations expiring in nine days. Wendell walks into the creek shallows and screams. Then, quietly: 'Then we have nine days.' Emotional beat: climax of trust forged through betrayal survived.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. An investigative montage: courthouse copies, a dying witness's taped statement, Junie unknowingly identifying the car from a drawing she made at age four. The Ashfords catch wind; pressure descends on the bookshop's lease. Emotional beat: rising tension, ticking clock, small-town walls closing in.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Mrs. Ashford offers Wendell anything—debt forgiven, Junie's college funded—if the past stays past, framing it as mercy for Junie's sake. Wendell sees his own years of silence reflected back and refuses. Emotional beat: temptation resisted; loyalty to the dead over comfort for the living.

chapters.title: The Town Tribunal
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. With courts barred by the statute, Marisol invokes Junebug Creek's obscure founding charter: a public reading of grievances at the grange hall. Half the town attends. The tape plays. Caleb, present, does not deny it—he confesses, hollowed out. Emotional beat: climax; justice rendered not by law but by witness.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Ashes and Soil
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The town fractures and mends unevenly; the Ashford name falls, and Wendell feels no triumph, only lightness. He reads Lian's letter aloud at her grave, finally saying goodbye instead of sorry. Emotional beat: catharsis; grief given its ending so love can have its beginning.

chapters.title: The Real Date
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. No contracts this time: Wendell asks Marisol to dinner properly, nervously, Junie supervising from the stairs. They talk about the future in specifics—a garden, a sign that says Zhou & Vega Books. Emotional beat: tenderness earned; the fake made true by choice rather than circumstance.

chapters.title: First Bloom
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Spring: Lian's garden blooms again, planted jointly by all three. Marisol hangs her shingle beside the bookshop—justice work, small cases, the town that watched her become both betrayer and healer. Emotional beat: belonging; second chances proven real for people brave enough to take them.

chapters.title: The Garden of Junebug Creek Anew
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, epilogue. One year later, at the next reunion, Wendell arrives holding Junie's hand and Marisol's, introduced not as a widower or a faker but simply as himself. His mother's toast names the theme: staying visible is the bravest thing a person can do. Emotional beat: resolution and resonance—the mirror finally shows a man he forgives.
